sources.citation: Morgan, Hope E. 2017. The Phonology of Kenyan Sign Language (Southwestern Dialect). PhD dissertation, University of California San Diego. 633 pp.

sources.note: Nothing. Full-text search (stress/accent/prominence/rhythm/intonation/emphasis) finds no statement about word stress or word-level prominence in KSL; 'stress' occurs only as the English gloss of the signs STRESS-1, STRESS-3, STRESSED. Prosody is treated only as feature geometry (Brentari 1998 Prosodic Model vs. Dependency Model) and, p.76, a recap of ASL rhythm studies (Allen et al. 1991; Wilbur & Allen 1991) that found no predictable syllable-internal rhythmic peak -- about ASL, not KSL.
